answer: Memory-hard minting resists sybils: each identity's mint puzzle must allocate and randomly traverse a large RAM buffer, so minting is bound by memory CAPACITY held simultaneously, not by cores. A wander through a thousand fakes needs a thousand large buffers resident at once; a lagoon of commodity RAM drains fast and cannot be time-shared without serializing the mints. The delta between an honest agent's single buffer and a farm's demand grows linearly with head count, so bulk creation pays real gigabyte-seconds per head and the economy-of-scale discount vanishes.
